card.name: Karma Naach
card.tagline: Tribal Karam-tree worship dance of fate and harvest
card.profile: Karma Naach (Karma dance) is a tribal folk dance of central and eastern India performed annually during the Karam (Karma) festival, in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal (Wikipedia; Prepp). Performed by communities including the Oraon, Munda, Ho, Santhal, Baiga and Gond, dancers form circles around a freshly cut branch of the sacred Karam tree (Nauclea parvifolia), arms around each other's waists, to worship Karam Devta/Karam-sani Devi - the deity of fate, fertility, youth and prosperity - seeking a good harvest. The festival falls on the 11th day of the bright fortnight of Bhadrapada (August-September) (Historified; Karma Naach Wikipedia).
card.insight: The largest Karma Naach dance, with 3,049 participants forming 61 circles of 50, was achieved by the District Administration Mandla in Madhya Pradesh on 11 April 2016, recognized by Guinness World Records.
card.image_significance: The dance of the fate-god's tree. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — central/eastern tribal, India.

observation.setting: on a stage indoors with a black backdrop featuring a stylized cat/mask design and the text 'ESCAPE THE ORDINARY PULSE WONDERLAND', under changing colored stage lights
observation.dancers: mixed group of men and women, numbering around eight to ten
observation.formation_and_space: group shifts between lines, semi-circles, scattered formations across the stage, and carrying one dancer on shoulders in pyramid/tower formations
observation.posture: upright torso with frequent forward upper body bends, flexed knees, and low stances
observation.footwork: fast-paced stepping, hopping, jumping on beats, running, and crouching low to the floor; exact weight transfers cannot be clearly determined from low-resolution frames
observation.arms_and_hands: arms swing, extend outward, hold props such as metal bowls, drums, and long sticks
observation.hips_and_torso: torso bends forward and upright; hips move in coordination with rhythmic stepping and bending
observation.partnering: lifting and supporting dancers into shoulder and pyramid formations; brief hand contact in circle/line sections
observation.levels_jumps_turns: frequent jumps, crouching floor-level dips, level changes between standing, squatting, and being lifted on shoulders
observation.costume_and_props: women wear red and gold traditional attire with head adornments; men wear yellow/striped vests over white dhotis/pants with red headbands; props include metal bowls/baskets, drums, and tall sticks
observation.cannot_infer: exact foot-to-floor weight transfer and intricate footwork detail are obscured by stage lighting changes, fast motion blur, and video compression

signature_moments.what: Dancers move in a line across the stage with dynamic arm swings and synchronized footwork while maintaining a low-kneed posture.
Female dancers balance metal bowls on their heads while performing rhythmic foot taps and graceful hand gestures.
Male dancers strap large horizontal drums to their waists and beat them energetically while jumping and turning.
